title: The printing press was never invented
premise: In 1440 Gutenberg's workshop fails and movable type never spreads. Books remain rare handwritten treasures, and powerful guilds of scribes and memorizers become the keepers of knowledge. Cities learn to speak, paint and remember together, building halls for recitation where libraries would have stood.

chain.event: In Mainz Gutenberg's press trials produce uneven type and lose funding, and movable type is set aside.
chain.consequence: Hand copying remains the only way to make books, keeping them costly and guarded by workshops.

chain.event: Cities charter powerful guilds of scribes and memorizers to license copying and public recitation.
chain.consequence: Scriptoria and recitation halls become civic centers and memory training becomes a honored craft.

chain.event: Teachers develop standard memory halls and picture-sign codes for law, craft and news.
chain.consequence: Ideas travel by trained reciters and painted image boards, allowing shared culture without printed text.

chain.event: Artisans perfect large stencil and relief presses that print pictures, seals and color patterns but not small text.
chain.consequence: Streets fill with vivid image posters and signboards while words stay handwritten, strengthening visual storytelling.

chain.event: Municipal Living Libraries open where citizens can consult reciters and copyists by the hour.
chain.consequence: Oral learning and hand copying become everyday public life, shaping schools, plazas and street architecture.

chain.event: The Concord of Reciters links cities by traveling memory festivals and illuminated public panels.
chain.consequence: Handmade knowledge culture stays vibrant and peaceful, honored in calm gathering places and glowing picture walls.

eras.caption: 1526 · Hall of Copied Voices
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 1526. Guild halls of scribes and memorizers in the region's own building tradition, their facades wrapped in hand-painted story friezes and hanging painted scribe signs. Copying benches and lecterns wait in shaded arcades under soft golden morning light.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A snug candle-lit copying room with long oak tables, stacked vellum, ink bowls and quills laid out for the day's work.

eras.caption: 1926 · City of Reciters
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 1926. Grand recitation houses in the region's own architectural style, their walls covered in large painted picture panels and enamel seal plaques. Stepped speaking platforms and festival banners fill the open spaces in clear midday sun.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A spacious recitation hall with polished wood benches in circles, warm lantern light and walls lined with painted scroll cabinets and listening niches.

eras.caption: 2026 · Living Library Streets
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 2026. Smooth limestone and cedar library arcades with living green roofs and broad glass doors, fronted by large illustrated public panels and bronze inkwell posts. Woven mats and reading benches line the walkways in gentle afternoon light.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A bright modern living-library interior with cedar shelves for handmade books, soft reading nooks and a central recitation circle under skylight glow.

eras.caption: 2126 · Glowing Memory Canopy
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 2126. Graceful limestone and light-timber pavilions with curved solar canopies, their facades set with softly glowing illustrated panels and living vine trellises. Quiet listening benches glow under calm pearly evening light.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A serene glowing memory chamber with curved timber walls, cushioned listening rings and luminous ceiling panels casting warm diffused light.

eras.caption: 3026 · Garden of Kept Stories
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 3026. Moss-softened limestone arcades and cedar pavilions, their roofs and balconies embraced by tall trees, flowering vines and herb gardens. Peaceful garden paths wind between them in dappled green daylight.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A sunlit garden hall where climbing plants frame cedar shelves of handmade books, with mossy stone benches and soft leaf-filtered light for quiet reading.
